notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; step 1 was correct.
No breadboard is used: the PIR sensor connects directly to the Pi's GPIO header with three female-to-female jumper cables.
The catalogue has no female-to-female jumper type (lookup returned only male-to-female), so the generic jumper-wire is used for the three cables.
Raspberry Pi model is not stated; raspberry-pi-3b is used because it is the catalogue Pi with named GPIO header pins and matches the full-size board in the image.
From the image, the red wire goes to the 5V pin at header position 2 (5V.1) and the black wire to the GND pin at position 6 (GND.1). The orange wire goes to GP4 (GPIO4) at position 7.
The PIR sensor is a 5V-powered part (supply 4.5-20 V on VCC), so 5V is correct. Its OUT signal is normally 3.3 V, which is safe for the Pi's GPIO input.
